svg.text: Figure 4. Where the slice-spacing effect sits inside Sybil: a signal from Sybil's own padding
NLST test, pre-registered (H2, H6, H7): mean change of Sybil's logit
as Sybil gives it, and with shared axis 0 switched off (set to its dev mean in all five members; nothing refitted)
mean change of the logit (z-fix minus as read; later minus earlier screen per stretch change)
Switching axis 0 off removes the mean shift, not the exam-by-exam scatter: z-fix exams whose 1-year logit moves >= 1/4 SD:
70.8% as Sybil gives it, 54.0% with axis 0 off. 1-year AUROC with axis 0 off minus as given: -0.0003 [-0.005, +0.003] (no change detected; secondary).
The z-fix moves axis 0 by -2.73 dev SD [-2.76, -2.70]; a change of stretch between yearly screens moves it by
2.39 dev SD [2.28, 2.50]. H7 is partly seen before the freeze; 121 of its 134 changed pairs involve GE.
Stretching normal scans on purpose: 48 non-overlapping dev scans, 12 per maker (exploratory; no outcome read)
Stretch factor f = how much longer Sybil sees the scan (f = 1: the scan as it is; f = 2: what Sybil does to a 50%-overlapping scan read with the wrong spacing)
change of the 1-year logit (blue) and its axis-0 part A0 (grey)
Axis 0 rises with f and stops once Sybil's 200-slice box is full (f = 2.5 minus f = 2.0 on the same 20 scans: +0.08 SD [+0.07, +0.10]). Axis 0 and A0 rise in all four makers; the total
1-year logit at f = 2 does not in every maker (Philips +0.06 [-0.32, +0.43]). Square: f = 2 cut back to the true scan's number of slices and padded like it keeps 2.8% [2.4, 3.1]

of the axis-0 shift (its logit, +0.53, is not read: the cut removes about half of the lung). Diamond: no stretch at all, only air instead of Sybil's padding: axis 0 +2.41 SD, 1-year logit +0.245 [+0.226, +0.265].
What the z-fix changes in real overlapping scans: 63 dev scans (GE 24, Philips 27, Siemens 12; weighted to the dev maker mix; exploratory; no outcome read)
Each row: the scan read with its true spacing minus the scan as Sybil reads it, with the empty ends of Sybil's 200-slice box filled in different ways
the empty box ends filled with air (-1,000 HU)
box ends filled with the scan mirrored; no constant slab
stretched scan cut back to the z-fix's slice count, then padded
not read (cut-back scan loses about half of the lung)
z-fix minus the cut-back stretched scan
not read (cut-back scan loses about half of the lung)
a real non-overlapping series of the same scans (36 scans)

Air padding keeps 14.6% [14.0, 15.2] of the axis-0 shift; mirrored anatomy removes 97.4%; at the same filling the stretch alone gives 2.2% [1.9, 2.6]. Every second slice gives 1.003 [1.002, 1.003] times the z-fix shift.
With air padding the mean logit change is near 0, but the exam-by-exam scatter stays (right column): air padding does not fix Sybil, and it moves ordinary scans
out of their usual range of axis 0. Grey rows: mirrored anatomy adds image content, and the cut-back scans lose about half of the lung, so only their axis-0 change is read.
One curve: axis 0 against the padding left in Sybil's box, all 7,336 dev scans as Sybil read them (no new run; exploratory; no outcome read)
Padded slices = slices of Sybil's 200-slice input that hold only padding (both ends together); 0 = the box is full
padded slices in Sybil's 200-slice box (> 80 drawn at 88)
At the same padding the three groups agree (17-24 slices: +1.63 and +1.64):
the curve depends on how much padding is left, not on why.
Contiguous scans: median 74 padded slices; 0.2% have 32 or fewer.
Other scans: 419 of 2,274 (18%) have 32 or fewer.
The steep part (about 16 to 48 padded slices) is where a thin slab
already moves the axis; a full box (0) gives the highest values.
Each point: mean axis 0 with its 95% participant-bootstrap interval; bins with fewer than 5 scans not drawn; points of a bin are spread sideways so they do not overlap.
